exercises.name: First Position Plié
instructions: Stand side-on to your support with heels together and toes turned out only as far as your hips allow.
Rest one hand lightly on the support and stand tall through the spine.
Bend your knees out over your toes, keeping your heels down and your torso upright.
Lower as far as you can with the heels on the floor, then press down and straighten slowly.
exercises.formCue: Knees over toes, tall spine, heels down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Forcing the feet wider than the hips can turn so the knees roll inward, or tipping the chest forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller turnout and a shallower bend, with both hands on the support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the basic barre knee bend and it trains the hips, knees, and feet to line up.

exercises.name: Second Position Plié
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than your hips and toes turned out, one hand resting on your support.
Lengthen your spine and keep your shoulders over your hips.
Bend your knees out over your toes and lower your hips straight down.
Stop when your thighs approach level or your form starts to change.
Press through your whole foot to rise and squeeze your inner thighs at the top.
exercises.formCue: Hips drop straight down between the heels.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees fall in front of the toes line, or sticking the hips back and leaning forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take a narrower stance and a smaller bend, holding the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide turned-out stance loads the inner thighs and glutes with little impact.

exercises.name: Relevé
instructions: Stand tall with feet parallel or heels together and one hand on your support.
Press through the balls of your feet and rise smoothly onto them.
Keep your ankles straight, with the weight over the big and second toes.
Pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Rise straight up, ankles stay in line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling out toward the little toes, or dropping down fast.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the support with both hands and rise only part way.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the calves and ankles and sharpens balance on the forefoot.

exercises.name: Plié Pulse
instructions: Set up in a wide turned-out stance with one hand on your support.
Lower into your plié and hold near the bottom.
Pulse up and down a few centimetres, staying low and keeping the knees over the toes.
Keep your torso upright and your breathing steady.
Finish the set, then press slowly to standing.
exercises.formCue: Small range, stay low, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing with a big range, or letting the knees drift inward as the legs tire.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the low position without pulsing, or stay higher in the bend.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Small pulses under tension build muscular endurance without any impact.

exercises.name: Tendu
exercises.musclesWorked: Feet, calves, hip stabilisers, inner thighs
instructions: Stand tall with heels together and one hand on your support.
Slide one foot along the floor to the front, side, or back until only the toes touch.
Keep both knees straight and your hips level and still.
Draw the foot back along the floor to the start, pressing through the ball of the foot.
Repeat in each direction, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Brush the floor out and back, hips quiet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the foot instead of sliding it, or shifting the hips toward the working leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work in parallel rather than turned out, and hold the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the feet and arches and teaches you to balance on one leg while the other moves.

exercises.name: Arabesque Lift
instructions: Face your support and hold it with both hands, standing tall.
Slide one leg straight back until the toes rest on the floor behind you.
Lift the leg a small way without tipping your chest forward or arching your back.
Pause, lower to tap the toes, and repeat.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Lift from the glute, keep the chest up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back or opening the hip to the side to lift higher.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only a few centimetres and bend the standing knee slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the glutes and trains balance on the standing leg.

exercises.name: Standing Side Leg Lift
instructions: Stand side-on to your support and rest one hand on it.
Stand tall with both hips facing forward.
Lift the outside leg out to the side with the toes pointing forward.
Go only as high as you can without leaning, then lower slowly.
Complete the reps and repeat on the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Body stays tall as the leg goes out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the lifting leg, or turning the toes up so the hip flexors take over.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift lower and hold the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the outer hip muscles that steady the pelvis when you walk and balance.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge Pulse
instructions: Stand tall and step one foot back and across behind the other leg.
Bend both knees and lower with your chest upright and front knee over the front heel.
Stay low and pulse up and down a few centimetres.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Finish the set and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, front knee over the heel.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the hips and letting the front knee collapse inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Skip the pulses, take a smaller step, and hold a support for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The crossed stance puts extra work into the glutes and outer hip of the front leg.

exercises.name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent, feet together, and head resting on your lower arm.
Stack your hips one over the other.
Keep your feet touching and lift the top knee without letting your hips roll back.
Pause, then lower the knee slowly.
Finish the reps and turn over for the other side.
exercises.formCue: Feet together, hips stacked, knee opens.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling the top hip backward, or opening so far that the pelvis moves.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lie with your back against a wall to stop the hips rolling, and use a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It targets the outer hip muscles that keep the knee and pelvis steady.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
instructions: Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent for balance and the top leg straight in line with your body.
Stack your hips and shoulders.
Lift the top leg just high enough to feel the outer hip working, toes pointing forward.
Lower slowly without resting between reps.
Complete the set and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the heel, hips stacked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling the hips back, or lifting so high that the waist does the work.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lie with your back against a wall and use a smaller lift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the outer hip with no load on the spine or knees.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your trunk and keep your back flat.
Keep the knee bent and lift one leg out to the side.
Pause briefly without letting your trunk rotate, then lower with control.
Finish the reps and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Leg moves, trunk stays square to the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the lifting leg, or letting the back sag or twist.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee only a little, or do the Clamshell instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the outer hips while the core works to keep the trunk still.

exercises.name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your trunk so your back stays flat.
Keep the knee bent and lift one leg, pressing the sole of the foot toward the ceiling.
Stop before your lower back starts to arch.
Lower with control, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze the glute, keep the back flat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too high and arching the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller range, or rest on your forearms.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the glutes on their own with the spine held steady.

exercises.name: Seated March
instructions: Sit upright away from the back of the chair with feet flat on the floor.
Hold the sides of the seat lightly.
Lift one knee as high as is comfortable, keeping the knee bent.
Lower the foot with control and lift the other knee.
Keep alternating at a steady rhythm, sitting tall.
exercises.formCue: Sit tall, lift the knee, place the foot down softly.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the knee lifts, or dropping the foot down hard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the heel only, or march more slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It raises the heart rate and works the hips with no balance demand.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension
instructions: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Slowly straighten one knee until the leg is level with the floor.
Hold for a moment with the thigh still on the seat.
Lower the foot slowly to the floor.
Finish the reps on one leg, then switch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the leg up, or slumping back as the leg lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Straighten only part way, or slide the heel along the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the front of the thigh from a fully supported seat.
